extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and reporters who write court and police news
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting criminal and civil court proceedings and police news: selecting leads, presenting testimony, including essential details (verdicts, sentences, decisions, histories, bankruptcy/will particulars), and avoiding sensationalism or prejudicial publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of court news
rubrics_metrics.description: To give fair and accurate publicity to significant phases of the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court proceedings are activities of important branches of government and matters of public concern; the writer's aim is to publicize significant phases fairly and accurately. Publicity of punishment also serves a deterrent function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience relevance (lead focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reporting sessions of these bodies, the writer's aim should be to direct the reader's attention to those details of the proceedings (1) that are significant to him personally, (2) that affect the interests of the community, and (3) that relate to the welfare of society as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose details and emphasis that connect with individual readers, community interest, and broader social welfare when determining the lead and focus of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of court news
rubrics_metrics.description: Court news covers such matters as police court news, criminal trials, civil suits, divorce suits, bankruptcy, wills and other probate court matters, decisions of higher courts, and findings of judicial officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the wide range of judicial procedure included under court news and adapt treatment accordingly (routine reports, decisions, probate matters, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of matter-of-fact informative story for routine court news
rubrics_metrics.description: Since much court news is of a routine character, the matter-of-fact informative news story is a frequent medium for presenting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine or procedural reports should favor clear, factual, concise presentation rather than melodrama; human-interest or narrative approaches may be used when the case has strong personal elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and value of human-interest treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal and civil cases often have a strong human interest element that, if rightly developed, may be a valuable part of the story; the little comedies and tragedies of the police court have long been favorite subjects for entertaining and appealing human interest stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, develop human interest angles to make court news appealing, but do so without sacrificing accuracy or becoming sensational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism / destructive or anti-social influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Destructive, or anti-social, influences are found in those court stories — particularly those of criminal and divorce cases — that play up disgusting or scandalous phases of such trials in order to gratify the morbid taste of some of their readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not emphasize repulsive or scandalous details solely to titillate readers; avoid degrading coverage that serves morbid curiosity rather than public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'trying the case in the newspaper' (prejudicial publicity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspapers should not undertake to prove the innocence or the guilt of an accused person by printing whatever evidence they can secure, even though some of it would be excluded from the trial under the rules of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from publishing prejudicial material or excluded evidence that creates public opinion and could prevent the accused from obtaining a fair trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of material (finding and presenting significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: To find matters of general significance and interest, particularly when they are buried in legal technicalities and verbiage, and to present them clearly and attractively without sacrificing accuracy, are the main problems in handling court news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract the salient points from legal documents and proceedings, translate technicalities into clear prose, and keep accuracy paramount while making the story accessible and engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead is usually determined by the status of the case. Any one of the important points may be made the feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide the lead based on what is most newsworthy given the case's stage or status (verdict, important testimony, decision, sentencing, new development) and make that angle the feature of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body composition of court stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The body of court news stories usually consists of summaries of arguments, decisions, testimony, or legal documents, or of excerpts from them, with the necessary connective material. In some instances the story is largely a history of the case or action and of the persons involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise summaries and selective excerpts tied together with connective context; include background/history when it helps readers understand significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony presentation formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony in news stories is given in one of three forms: (1) the question indicated by "Q" and the answer by "A," both question and answer given in one paragraph without quotation marks, (2) the question and the answer in quotation marks, each followed by the necessary explanatory matter and each in a separate paragraph, (3) a summary of the testimony of each witness in indirect quotation form, with the name of the witness at or near the beginning of the first sentence of the summarized testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the testimony format that best serves clarity and readability; ensure attribution and necessary explanatory material accompany quoted or summarized testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include verdict and conditions under which it was rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (1) the verdict and the conditions under which it was rendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the verdict and any relevant context (e.g., jury deliberation length, hung jury, plea agreements, special conditions) that affected how the verdict came about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the sentence imposed
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (2) the sentence imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the sentence, include relevant modifiers (suspended, concurrent, probation terms), and note factors cited in sentencing where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include decision rendered and its significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (3) the decision rendered and its significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the court's ruling and why it matters — legal precedent, public policy implications, or effects on parties/community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include important testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (4) important testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight key witness statements that influenced outcomes, summarizing them accurately and attributing properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include net results of the day's proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (5) net results of the day's proceedings in a trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize what changed as a result of that day's proceedings (e.g., witness testimonies received, rulings on motions, postponements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include history of the case or action
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (6) the history of the case or action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide succinct background so readers understand the context and how the case reached its present stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include provisions of a will when reporting probate
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (7) provisions of a will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report key bequests, executors named, and any contested provisions or unusual dispositions that affect public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include liabilities, assets, and cause in bankruptcy reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (8) liabilities, assets, and cause in bankruptcy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the financial picture and the reasons for bankruptcy filings when relevant to public or creditor interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the award or finding
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (9) the award, or finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report judgments, damages awarded, or official findings clearly, including amounts and basis for awards if pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include grounds on which a suit is based
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the important details are (10) the grounds on which a suit is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the legal basis of the claim (e.g., negligence, breach of contract) in plain language so readers grasp the core allegation.
